groups.compat: Required to run outside a team-signed iPhone/iPad install (PlayCover/macOS) and without the dead content bucket.
groups.privacy: Stops ad and cross-promotion SDKs (and their network traffic). Independent of any server.
groups.offline: Runs without Ubisoft/RedLynx services. Replace this group, not the others, if a fan server appears.
groups.story-extras: Small additions to the story: mission 507 (see docs/MISSIONS.md). On by default: a build without it would crash the Saloon for a save that has the mission on offer.

Always return the existing constant @"unknown" (CFString at 0x100d73c38) instead; execution falls through to the function's normal cleanup/return at 0x100adb2a8.

Only place that reads the Ads_enabled / Interstitials_enabled settings and starts the ad SDKs (AdMob rewarded video + 'Trials Interstitial End Run' interstitial, Tapjoy, Domob). Returning immediately is equivalent to Ads_enabled = 0, a configuration the game supports; tr::AdInterface::init() is a tail call to it. Stops ad SDK network traffic and ad views under PlayCover.
Decides from play counters alone and never checks that an ad SDK was initialised; always answer false so the game never attempts an interstitial (e.g. at the end of a run).
Always report no rewarded video available, so the game does not offer watch-an-ad rewards that can no longer work.

Downloadable packs (TrialsContentDL.dat, TrialsContentDL2.dat, TrialsContentOfferDL.dat) came from https://s3.amazonaws.com/dlcontent_frontier_ios/<version>/info.json; that bucket no longer exists, and isDLReady() is false whenever the saved download state (Caches/dl_content.state) is empty. After the early mission set by DLContent_Lock_MissionId the game then blocks on 'Download needed - Please Wait'. Report content as ready; the game already tolerates the packs being absent (fresh installs run the tutorial without them). All callers (main menu, weekly challenge, daily reward, ad interface, command queue) go through this function.

replacement_asm: ldr x24, [x8, #0x570] ; sel currentMode (kept for later code)
ldr x25, [x8, #0x578] ; sel size (kept for later code)
bl objc_msgSend ; [screen nativeBounds] -> d0..d3 = x, y, w, h
patches.reason: The engine's screen size (mz::SystemInit::init -> 0x100f2ada0, used for UI layout and raw glScissor rectangles) comes from [[UIScreen mainScreen] currentMode].size, which is in pixels on iOS. PlayTools hooks UIScreenMode.size and, with a custom resolution, returns the window size in points, so scissor rectangles (Gfx::Transform::setScissor, e.g. in MenuzComponentScroller) cover only the bottom-left quarter of the 2x framebuffer. Read the size from [UIScreen mainScreen].nativeBounds instead (pixels on iOS; PlayTools reports window size x scale). The code already orders the two values as max/min, so nativeBounds' portrait orientation does not matter. x24/x25 still hold the currentMode/size selectors as before.

Ubisoft's config gateway (gamecfg-mob.ubi.com -> houston-services) still answers, and after the nickname step the game would run a 'silent login' that creates/links a Ubisoft profile '#TF-<nickname>'. Silent-login keyboard mode exists only to build '#TF-<name>' names for auto-created Ubisoft accounts (disabled by offline-mode). In that mode the OK handler (PopupStateKeyboard::componentReleased) assigns "#TF-" into an mt::String whose buffer is the shared read-only "" literal; this only works because the 4-char prefix forces a heap allocation (an empty prefix crashed with KERN_PROTECTION_FAILURE). Using the ordinary name keyboard (as for renames) skips that path. Side effect: no 3-letter / bad-word validation; the accept button still requires a non-empty name.

Pre-fill the nickname keyboard with the bare stored name instead of '#TF-' + name. The literal is copied into a std::string (no in-place write), and with an empty prefix the prepend branch is skipped.

patches.function: C string used by MobileSDKAPI::msdk_internal_InitThread (and a global pointer at 0x100f29cc0)
patches.reason: Ubisoft Mobile SDK's base URL. Its init also sets up local state (sqlite DB, IAP store data), so keep the init and point the URL at a closed local port so requests fail immediately. Same-length-or-shorter string, read-only use (passed as a parameter).

Some texture slots are reserved but never set up because their pack (the downloadable TrialsTexturesDL.dat) is gone; e.g. tr::BgRenderer::renderBackDrop on tracks whose backdrop uses such textures (desert rocks etc.). bindTexture lazily loads via the Texture's vtable and crashed on the null vtable (KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0, seen loading a level with the restored iPad profile). If the vtable is null, skip loading and still call TEXTURE_HW::bind on the empty hardware texture (binds nothing), so the object is just invisible. Cave in the Mach-O header padding after the gem caves.

After every login (OnlineCore::onAuthenticationComplete) the game compares the logged-in profile with the save's owner; if they differ it saves the current progress as player_<owner hash>.prgstore, resets the player and loads player_<new hash>.prgstore if there is one (multi-account support). With local services each game copy has exactly one account; a different profile only arrives by mistake, e.g. when two copies run at once and the second reaches the first one's server on port 7979 (seen 2026-10-14: two copies were reset to new players). Never switch: always take the same-account path and keep the save.

Only loopback traffic for the game's own HTTP layer. _NETWORK_makeRequest (every engine request: Ubiservices, game server, configuration, images, store, offers) used getNetworkType() as its gate; this cave instead allows the request only if its URL starts with "http://127.0.0.1:", independent of the offline group. Anything else fails locally exactly as with no network (nativeGotError 5). This is the guarantee that re-enabled online code paths cannot reach the internet.

replacement_asm: adrp x16, 0x100d03000; ldr x16, [x16, #0xa0]; br x16  ; real getaddrinfo (GOT)
patches.function: code cave for the _getaddrinfo symbol stub
patches.reason: Hard stop for every other network stack in the executable that resolves names itself: libcurl (Ubisoft mobile login library: account/ticket POSTs, network time; content checks), the ubiservices C++ SDK sockets, GCDAsyncUdpSocket, SNTP. The getaddrinfo symbol stub jumps to a cave that calls the real getaddrinfo only for the host "127.0.0.1" and returns EAI_NONAME (8) for anything else, so no DNS lookup or connection to another host can start. (NSURLSession/NSURLConnection resolve inside CFNetwork; the engine path is covered by the loopback-only hook, the SDK paths by the privacy group.)

patches.reason: The results popup keeps its own copies of the leaderboards it showed (including the player's own entry and name) and drops them only when the hash it keeps changes; that was the profile id, which a new player keeps when they pick their name in the tutorial, so boards first loaded before naming (the Hall of Fame, the tutorial's first tracks) kept showing the old placeholder for the rest of the session. Hashing the name instead drops them when the name changes (offline there is one profile, whose name changes at most on renaming).

Map::init calls Map::cheatOpenAllLevels only when its bool argument is set (a developer switch). That function reveals the marker of every level with LevelMetaData::isAvailableOnMap (X^2+Y^2 < 8000^2) and a name localization, i.e. 370 of 382 levels (the 6 parked at -10000,-10000 and 6 unnamed test levels stay hidden). Always take that path. Markers only; progress, missions and the save are not changed (a level becomes permanently opened once it has a time).

patches.function: code cave for __getSaveFilePath(mt::String const&, unsigned char) type 6
patches.reason: The game opens texture packs that are not in its built-in table, and downloaded content packs, only from its download folder: __getSaveFilePath type 6 = NSCachesDirectory + "/DLC" (tr::GlobalData::findFilePacks). iOS may purge Caches, the game's DLContentManager may delete files there, and a sideloaded app has no installer to put packs there. Make type 6 resolve to [[[NSBundle mainBundle] resourcePath] stringByAppendingString:@"/DLC"] instead (bundle: never purged, read-only); scripts/build_ipa.py puts the packs into TrialsFrontier.app/DLC (see bundle_dlc). The cave uses only references the game already has: NSBundle classref 0x100ed9560, selrefs mainBundle 0x100ec1080 and stringByAppendingString: 0x100ec1530, CFString @"/DLC" 0x100d70f18, stubs objc_msgSend 0x100ae1dc0 and sel_registerName 0x100ae2120 (for "resourcePath", which has no selref).

tr::BikeUpgrade::getBikeStatus(bike) is the one place that decides whether a bike is unlocked (43 callers: garage, bike selection, rewards, slot machine): 0 (ready) when the blueprint-part counter, item (0x48 + bike) sub 4, has reached the bike's requirement (BikeUpgradeData+0x58, "BP" 4-50), -1 while collecting, -2 without parts. Here x8 = the bike's BikeUpgradeData (tier at +0x3b: 0-2, 0xff special, 0xfe = not in the bike data, e.g. the unused ids 20 and 21, left alone), w19 = the bike id. Legendary = the bikes whose garage text is M_GARAGE_BIKE_LEGENDARY_TIER1-3 in 7.9.0's bike data: ids 13, 14, 16, 17, 18 (mask 0x76000). The three unlock groups hook three consecutive instructions, each returning 0 for its own bikes and otherwise running the replaced instruction, so any combination works. This one: tier 0-2 and not legendary. Cave in the Mach-O header padding.

Story veterans: a one-time marker, item 126 sub 0 (unused by the game, saved with all 280 items), set when the patched game first meets a save: 2 if Butch's finale (mission 212, solved flag Player+0x3280+212 bit 0) is already done, else 1. Runs at the single exit of Player::checkPlayerProfileVersion (every load, new players included, and main menu activations; x19 = Player); acts only while the marker is 0 (stored form rol(0,7)^0xab1d4f5), then sets the 'save needed' bit Player+0x6de4 as the game does after its own version write. Mission 507 requires marker >= 2, so only players who finished the story before meeting the patch see it.

plist_patches.reason: Facebook SDK auto-logs app activation (graph.facebook.com) when the app becomes active, independent of the removed FBSDKApplicationDelegate call. Facebook's documented opt-out key.
iOS has no other way for a player to copy the game's data off the device (deleting the app deletes it).

App Store thinning writes the model list of the device family it was downloaded for into UISupportedDevices (an iPad copy lists only iPads), and iOS refuses to install the app on anything else (MIInstallerErrorDomain 86, DeviceNotSupportedByThinning). The unthinned app has no such key and declares UIDeviceFamily [1, 2] (iPhone and iPad).

optional_groups.unlimited-fuel: Races never use fuel (tr::ConsumableManager::isUnlimitedFuel). Without it the game's own fuel and refill timer work offline.
optional_groups.unlimited-gems: Gems always read 9999; spending lowers the real balance (never below 0) and earned gems still add to it. Without it the game's own gems.
optional_groups.local-services: Opt-in (build with --with local-services). Talks to a local game-services server on http://127.0.0.1:7979 for login, leaderboards and ghosts. The game's HTTP layer may only reach 127.0.0.1 and getaddrinfo resolves only 127.0.0.1, so nothing leaves the machine. Use together with the offline group.
optional_groups.coins-for-gems: Opt-in (build with --with coins-for-gems). The six coin packs are App Store purchases (com.ubisoft.redlynx.trialsfrontier.caps1-6) that cannot work any more; turn them into ordinary gem-priced shop items, priced like the gem pack of the same price tier (diamonds1-6). A content edit made at build time in the user's own content.dat; nothing from the game is shipped.
optional_groups.unlock-bikes: Opt-in (build with --with unlock-bikes). The regular bikes of tiers 1-3 (the game's tiers 0-2: Armadillo, Tango, Bronco, Jackal, Mantis, Marauder, Riptide, Berserker, Phantom, Bandito) count as unlocked, whatever blueprint parts the save has. The game's own garage check (UpgradeManager::checkForUnlockedBikes) records them in the save the first time the garage opens, with upgrades at level 0; upgrade them in the game. The three unlock groups are independent and can be combined.
optional_groups.unlock-legendary-bikes: Opt-in (build with --with unlock-legendary-bikes). The legendary bikes, ordinary tier bikes the garage labels legendary (sponsor/event bikes whose blueprint parts came from events): KTM 500 EXC, KTM 450 RALLY, BMW F800 GS, HD and HD EV. Recorded in the save like unlock-bikes.
optional_groups.unlock-special-bikes: Opt-in (build with --with unlock-special-bikes). The special bikes (tier 255 in the bike data, with their own leaderboards): Stallion (horse), BMW, Moonrover (jetpack) and Donkey. Recorded in the save like unlock-bikes.
optional_groups.open-all-levels: Opt-in (build with --with open-all-levels). Every named level inside the map circle is shown on the map, using the game's own developer function Map::cheatOpenAllLevels: event, season, X-Games and Bunker tracks that can no longer be unlocked. Levels with event rules may behave oddly.
optional_groups.orphan-levels: Opt-in (build with --with orphan-levels). Gives the six levels parked off the map at (-10000,-10000) a place in the main map's fogged area east of the eastern sea route (x 1230, artwork but no levels): Sine City, Hill Climb, Bunnyhop (hidden Bunker tracks), Rigged Roadway, Roadway (Agent event), Collapsed Orchard (Rodeo). They show up once opened, or with open-all-levels.
optional_groups.dev-levels: Opt-in (build with --with dev-levels; best with open-all-levels). Six unnamed developer/test levels that ship with the game (their level files are in the LevelPack1/2 packs) get a display name '<name> (dev)' and a spot in the fogged area east of the eastern sea route, below the orphan levels.
optional_groups.embedded-server: Opt-in, with local-services (build with --with local-services,embedded-server and build_ipa.py --inapp <dir with libTFLocalServices.dylib>). The game loads the native local services (inapp/, built by scripts/build_inapp.py) from its Frameworks folder and serves itself on 127.0.0.1:7979: nothing runs outside the app, on macOS (PlayCover) or iOS. Without this group, local-services expects an external server (server/local_services.py or tfserver) for development.
optional_groups.file-sharing: Opt-in (meant for iPhone/iPad installs). Shows the game's Documents folder (save, ghosts, LocalServices store) in Finder and the Files app, so players can back it up or copy it to another device.

content_patches.reason: Coin packs caps1-6 (60k, 150k, 360k, 750k, 1.65M, 5M coins) have no in-game price (PH 0, PS 0) and an App Store product ID, so the shop needs StoreKit and shows the network message. With the ID emptied and a hard (gem) price set they are bought like the gem-priced track packs (StoreItemManager::tryPurchaseItem -> purchaseItem). Gem prices = gems in the gem pack of the same tier (diamonds1-6: 200, 450, 600, 1000, 2200, 5800). The edited file is appended to the pack and only its index entry is repointed (scripts/datapack.py).

LevelMetaData::isAvailableOnMap is X^2+Y^2 < 8000^2; these six sit at (-10000,-10000). Main-map background tiles are 512 units, tile (row r, col c) at x = -1792 + 512c, y = -768 + 512r (Map::render), with art for rows 0-4, cols 0-6. The strip right of the eastern sea route (levels end near x 1100) has art but no levels, so it stays fogged (Map::renderOffscreenFogOfWar lights ~300 units around each revealed marker). Placed in a two-column zigzag (x 1180/1290, y -230 + 90 per row; rows 0-5 here, 6-11 for dev-levels): a user screenshot (about 0.6 px per map unit) shows the right-hand UI panel covering x > ~1370 at the camera limit. The four PvP special tracks keep bike tier 255 (any bike); see orphan-levels-any-bike-*.
The six test levels share two map spots (-832,572 and -141,1342) and some lie under other markers; move them to rows 6-11 of the orphan column.

edits.name: BACK FROM THE DEAD
edits.desc: Well, well, well... look who's back!|The whole {c1}Frontier{c0} went dark on {c1}June 30th, 2023.{c0} Lights out. Nothing but a black void.|Funny thing is, it was kind of peaceful. Just... nothing. No races, no Rider, no Butch.|But now that I'm back, I never want to go to that place again.|And look at you, back from the dead too! Not much worse for wear...|But I bet you're rusty! Better hop on that bike and start practicing again!|Me? I'm still minding my own business... mostly.|I swear on my mother's bunions, I've got something for you. For old times' sake.
edits.reward: That's for the memories, Rider.|Now get out there and keep the {c1}Frontier{c0} alive!|And save a ghost or two for old Butch, would ya?

bundle_dlc.note: build_ipa.py copies into the app's DLC/ folder every bundled TrialsTexturesDL*.dat that is not in the texture table, untabled content packs under a free dlc_content_alias_slots name, and the player's own downloaded packs (--dlc-from); the same selection install_playcover.py used for Library/Caches/DLC (scripts/dlcpacks.py).
